questions.q: What is the raw zone's job?
options: To hold the final, business-ready aggregated tables
To hold data after it has already been joined and aggregated
To store only validated and deduplicated data
To hold an exact, untouched copy of the source data, as ground truth you can always go back to
questions.explain: Nothing is validated or reshaped in raw — it exists purely as an unmodified reference.

questions.q: What happens to data in the cleansed zone?
options: Nothing changes — cleansed is identical to raw
The data is deleted after 30 days
Data is aggregated into daily summaries
Types are enforced, invalid rows are removed or flagged, duplicates handled, and it's converted to an analytics-friendly format
questions.explain: Cleansed data is trustworthy and typed, but still at roughly the same grain as the source — not yet aggregated.

questions.q: What does the curated zone typically contain?
options: The exact same untouched files as the raw zone
Business-ready data, aggregated and joined, shaped around a specific question a dashboard or report would query directly
A backup copy of the cleansed zone with no changes
Only raw, unvalidated data
questions.explain: Curated is the zone shaped for direct consumption by BI tools or reports.

questions.q: Why should raw data never be modified, even after discovering a problem with it?
options: There is no real reason — it's just a stylistic convention
Modifying raw data is technically impossible in Azure
Raw data is legally required to be immutable in all cases
If a cleansing rule turns out to be wrong, raw needs to still be there, complete, so you can reprocess correctly — modifying it in place would permanently lose that ability
questions.explain: Keeping raw untouched preserves the ability to redo downstream processing correctly if something was wrong.

questions.q: How does Lesson 12's Bronze/Silver/Gold relate to this lesson's Raw/Cleansed/Curated?
options: Bronze/Silver/Gold has four zones instead of three
Bronze/Silver/Gold replaces the need for a raw zone entirely
It's the same three-zone idea, popularized by Databricks and Delta Lake, with different vocabulary for the same underlying pattern
They are completely unrelated concepts
questions.explain: Different ecosystems, same underlying pattern — Lesson 12 covers exactly where they converge.
